name: genesis-games
content:
.TH GENESIS-GAMES 7 "November 2026" "Genesis 0.2.0" "Genesis Manual"
.SH NAME
genesis-games \- the arcade in Genesis's outer world
.SH SYNOPSIS
.nf
.B /arcade
.fi
.SH DESCRIPTION
The arcade is part of Genesis's outer world. It offers interactive
ARC-AGI-3 environments through the official Python
.B arc-agi
toolkit. The arcade is an environment interface, not a separate
cognitive system: observations pass through the world's perception
path, and actions pass through its action path.
.PP
Genesis may choose to play through her play urge or use the registered
arcade tools. The
.B /arcade
command reports available games and remembered play.
.SH OFFICIAL TOOLKIT
The toolkit's
.B Arcade
class discovers environments and opens game sessions. Genesis announces
the arcade at startup without initializing the toolkit. The toolkit is
loaded lazily when she explicitly requests the catalogue or enters a
game; this avoids creating an empty official scorecard on every Genesis
startup. A scorecard is run-scoped, while Genesis's learned per-game
memory is saved in her local world state and can survive restarts.
These are separate records and must not be treated as the same score.
If the package is unavailable or the service cannot be reached, the
arcade records the error and the rest of Genesis can continue.
.PP
Install the official toolkit with:
.nf
pip install arc-agi
.fi
.PP
The official API is hosted at
.UR https://three.arcprize.org
.UE .
The toolkit source and API documentation are maintained at
.UR https://github.com/arcprize/ARC-AGI
.UE .
.SH OPERATION MODES
The
.B GENESIS_ARC_MODE
environment variable selects the toolkit operation mode. Genesis
defaults this variable's effective value to
.B online
when it is not set; the official toolkit itself defaults to
.B NORMAL
when used directly without a mode.
.TP
.B online
Remote environments through the official API. This is Genesis's
default and is the mode for online scorecard activity.
.TP
.B normal
The toolkit's normal mode, which can use local and remote
environments.
.TP
.B offline
Local environments only. Only games available in the local
environment cache can be opened.
.TP
.B competition
The toolkit's competition mode applies its competition-specific
remote-play and scorecard restrictions. Confirm the official rules
before treating a run as a competition submission.
.PP
Set
.B ARC_API_KEY
in the environment to use a registered API key. Without a key, the
toolkit may obtain an anonymous key, which can expose fewer games.
Do not put the key in source code, logs, or command-line arguments.
.SH PLAYING
The arcade can list offered games, open a game, observe the board,
make an action, play a bounded bout, and leave a game while retaining
its learned memory.
.PP
The official toolkit exposes game actions such as
.B RESET
and
.BR ACTION1 " through " ACTION7 .
.B ACTION6
is coordinate-based; Genesis selects a detected shape and passes its
coordinates to the toolkit. Coordinates must be within the toolkit's
64-by-64 action coordinate range.
.PP
Game observations may contain multiple frames, the current state,
available actions, completed-level count, and total win-level count.
Genesis converts the latest frame to a grid for perception. The
official environment remains authoritative for the actual game state.
.SH STRUCTURAL LATENT DECODER
Each ARC board is passed through
.B worlds.games.latent.ArcEnvironmentDecoder
alongside Genesis's existing parietal grid and scene parser. The decoder
validates the 0–15 grid, extracts connected same-color components,
canonicalizes object order, records centroids, bounding boxes, shape
signatures and local Betti numbers (beta-0 components and beta-1
enclosed holes under the declared 4/8 connectivity convention), and
constructs a sparse directed adjacency graph. It produces a fixed
51-coordinate structural feature
vector containing board dimensions, occupancy, object statistics,
topological counts, spatial distribution, ranked object sizes/radii,
and color frequencies.
.PP
The vector is an interpretable feature embedding, not a pretrained or
learned neural embedding. The attributed graph is retained alongside it;
the vector does not replace object-level evidence. Background defaults
to the most common grid color, using the parietal parser's canonical
rule; callers may supply an explicit background when the environment
establishes one. The feature state is projected into the typed
experiential outer domain
.BR E .
Perception events carry the latent vector, uncertainty, object summary,
and current action-model evidence into the world's normal perception
path.
.PP
For each observed action, the decoder compares the before and after
latent states and updates local action-conditioned transition statistics.
Predictions are made only from a sufficiently nearby previously observed
state/action context. Welford running statistics estimate diagonal transition
uncertainty; uncertainty is not reduced merely because an action was
attempted.
When a prediction is available, its distance from the next observed
state is reported as
.B latent_prediction_error
in the perception metadata. These empirical models are saved inside
per-game world memory.
.PP
Goal evidence records observed level changes and the official terminal
state. The
.B GoalAttractorManifold
represents an explicitly supplied goal center and constant positive-definite metric tensor. Its satisfaction test measures membership in a
specified metric neighborhood; it does not manufacture a target from
reward or infer a win. The
.B LatentState.geodesic_distance
uses the exact constant-metric expression
.nf
d(x,y) = sqrt((y-x)^T G (y-x))
.fi
This is a geodesic only for the declared constant metric on that
coordinate chart; no varying Riemannian metric is claimed. The official
toolkit remains authoritative for level completion and wins.
.SH LEARNING AND MEMORY
Genesis keeps per-game memory in her world state. It includes action
effect counts, board visits, action-value estimates, moves and paths
that led to later levels. A temporal-difference update uses
.nf
delta = reward + gamma * max(Q(next_state, action)) - Q(state, action)
.fi
The resulting prediction error can influence the arcade's
neurochemical impulse path. The stored values are Genesis's learning
signals, not an official ARC-AGI-3 score.
.PP
The arcade routes board perception and actions through the outer
world, records arcade transitions through the active cognitive
journal, and exposes current play telemetry in
.BR /arcade .
Telemetry includes visits, remembered games, moves, wins, current
game and level, state, and the last error.
.SH DATA AND RECORDINGS
Arcade memory is serialized with the world's saved state. Arcade
events are sent to Genesis's active cognitive journal when one is
attached. This implementation does not establish
.I <data>/arc/results.jsonl
as the arcade's own output path; do not assume that file exists.
.PP
The official toolkit separately supports JSONL game recordings and
scorecard operations. Its recording directory and scorecard behavior
are controlled by the toolkit configuration, not by Genesis's
cognitive-journal path.
.SH LIMITATIONS
The structural feature coordinates are hand-designed, deterministic
descriptors. Their diagonal variance describes transition-model
uncertainty, not pixel-detection confidence or a full covariance matrix. They are not learned semantic concepts,
persistent object identity tracking, or a complete physical simulator.
Components use four-way same-color connectivity with the inferred or
explicit background color; enclosed holes use the complementary
eight-neighbor convention. The transition model is local empirical
evidence, not a globally valid dynamics law. The current transition
uncertainty is diagonal and does not represent a full covariance matrix.
Unknown actions or distant latent contexts produce no prediction.
.PP
The
.B TransitionOperator
and
.B DifferentiableOperatorSpace
types implement explicitly declared affine vector fields
.BR f(x)=Ax+b ,
their application, and their Lie bracket. Closure validation checks
whether pairwise brackets lie in the declared coefficient span. These
operators are a mathematical facility, not a fabricated interpretation
of ARC action identifiers: the official actions remain opaque discrete
controls and are not automatically promoted to differentiable vector
fields. Completion is grounded in the toolkit's terminal state, not a
Euclidean target-vector threshold. No claim is made that this decoder
alone solves ARC-AGI-3. It supplies structured observations and
measurable transition hypotheses to the existing memory, reasoning,
and action-selection faculties.
.SH DIAGNOSTICS
Use
.B /arcade
to inspect the catalogue and remembered play. If no games are offered,
check that
.B arc-agi
is installed, the selected operation mode is valid, network access is
available for remote modes, and
.B ARC_API_KEY
is configured if registered access is needed.
.PP
For official API behavior, modes, scorecards, and recordings, consult
the linked toolkit documentation. The toolkit API and competition
rules can change independently of Genesis.
.SH SEE ALSO
.BR genesis (1),
.BR genesis-browser (7),
.BR genesis-cli (1),
.BR genesis-daemon (8),
.BR genesis-math (7),
.BR genesis-reasoning (7),
.BR genesis-retina (1)
.SH AUTHOR
Genesis project
